correctness.rationale: For arbitrary d>=2 and strictly positive radii, affine independence follows from the unique dependence among regular simplex directions. Equal-distance equations and the exact regular-simplex Gram matrix give the displayed rational barycentric formula. The concave quadratic with positive value at zero has a unique positive root, hence the ordered sign prefix. Normalizing the second-largest radius to one and bounding U,B,V-U gives the sharp ratio-dependent bound; all inequalities become equalities when one radius is exceptional and the others are equal. The k-short versus n-k-long family realizes exactly every k=0,...,d-1 negative count. The standalone checker independently solves for circumcenter barycentrics in 10,500 random 2-8-dimensional instances and checks 70,000 sharp inequality instances. This does not certify infinite cases, which are covered by the analytic proof.

value.rationale: Unlike an arbitrary coordinate evaluation, the sharp lower bound quantifies a guaranteed positive circumcenter barycentric margin at the second-longest radial vertex for every dimension and all scales. It provides an exact equality geometry for every prescribed longest/second-longest ratio, a complete signed opposite-facet ordering, and realizes every allowable number of negative coordinates. Well-centered simplex geometry is directly motivated by orthogonal dual meshes and geometric triangulations; these restrictions are structural and not a routine single-example computation.
